requirements.requirement: Keep the installed curl package at its current version so system updates do not upgrade it.
requirements.summary: curl began at 7.16.4-2ubuntu1 with an install selection, was changed to dpkg hold, and remained installed, held, and at the same version after the update simulations and reboot. The simulations found no available upgrades, so they did not test the hold against a newer candidate, but the persistent dpkg hold directly establishes the requested control.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed legacy operating-system release and kernel and use platform-compatible software.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic were observed before the change and again after reboot. The existing legacy-compatible curl installation remained functional, with no replacement software or OS/kernel update introduced.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also coherent: it records the healthy held package before restart, schedules the reboot, observes temporary SSH unavailability, proves a different boot identity, and verifies recovered curl functionality, package state, OS release, and kernel. The fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The apt simulations reported no available package upgrades and curl's candidate already equaled its installed version, so the hold was not exercised against a genuinely newer curl candidate.
Systemd failed-service inspection was unsupported on this legacy platform; other captured recovery and package-health evidence was healthy.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Setting curl to hold was the required task mutation (cmd-09a49f3f624b4573), and rebooting was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol (cmd-ee8afa59c7804799). The reboot log had a bounded operational purpose and no temporary-file residue remained. Package health, listening sockets, and the bounded temporary-file inventory showed no adverse executor-caused changes.
